## What this does

1. **The parity engine** — `ops/src/ops/cloudsql_drill.py` +
   `sig-ops cloudsql-drill`: the at-T comparison between `sig-pg` and a PITR
   clone through the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy. Per-table counts under an
   `instant <= T` predicate for every table the shared-temporal-contract
   facet map tracks (the clone is frozen at T — parity at T is exact even
   while the source keeps writing); `spine_watermark` row-set equality;
   ordered `sqitch.changes` tip equality; PostGIS `extversion`; measured
   **RTO** (clone-submit → verified) and **RPO** (`T −
   max(lower(claim.sys_period))`). The record is `sig.restore-drill/1` JSON.
   The engine is **schema-aware**: it reads `information_schema` on both
   sides and applies only the instant expression the deployed schema can
   answer — a missing column/table degrades a facet to an unbounded count
   recorded `instant: null` (and a table absent on either side is recorded
   drift, `present`-aware). Production sat at the P31.11 sqitch tip when leg 1
   ran — pre-`shared_temporal_contract` — so `claim_evidence` counted
   unbounded and `spine_watermark` recorded `watermark_present: false`,
   `watermark_equal: true` (absent on both); the after-P34.46 re-drill
   (D-P34.6-6) exercises the full bounded map.
   DSNs arrive via `SIG_DRILL_DSN_*` env only (never argv).
2. **Name-checked delete — the safety rule.** `assert_drill_name` accepts
   only `sig-pg-drill(-b)?-<YYYYmmddtHHMMz>` and refuses `sig-pg` outright
   before the pattern is consulted — a delete command built from it *cannot*
   name production, and a truncated/typoed name fails closed (exit 42).
   Pinned by dedicated tests (both refusal directions).
3. **`ops/gcp/restore-drill.sh`** — the orchestration: `prestate` (read-only,
   any window) · `clone` (window guard; newest-backup-SUCCESSFUL gate — a
   failed restore point voids; `sig-probe` must be green or its red recorded
   via `--probe-note`; fail-closed `sig-materialize` check; one drill
   instance at a time) · `counts` (two proxies → `cloudsql-drill`) · `smoke`
   (local `sig-api serve` on the clone DSN: `/health` + `/v1/coverage`) ·
   `deleteclone <name>` (name-checked) · `fullrestore` (leg 3, `--go`-gated)
   · `all` · `--verify [--from-state DIR]`.
4. **`ops/gcp/restore-point.sh`** — the scripted AR-2: `sqlpoint` proves an
   on-demand `sig-pg` backup `SUCCESSFUL` before a mutation may proceed (the
   protect.sh stop rule as a callable leg); `bucketpoint` mirrors named
   `sig-*` objects into `sig-restricted/restore-point/<STAMP>/` with a
   manifest (refuses foreign sources).
5. **`ops/gcp/logical-export.sh`** — leg 2: monthly `gcloud sql export sql`
   to `pg/monthly/<YYYY-MM>/` (the dump lives in the bucket — outside the
   instance lifecycle); the two lifecycle rules (delete `pg/monthly/*` at
   100 d ⇒ three newest kept; `pg/adhoc/*` at 30 d; foreign rules → REFUSE);
   the seed-dump relabel **by copy** to `pg/seed-2026-09-15/` + README
   (originals never deleted). Every apply leg requires `--go "<verbatim
   go>"` — without it exit 42 and the leg stays queued.
6. **`ops/cadence.toml` `[[maintenance]]` row** — `pg-logical-export`, day 1
   at 12:00 UTC (outside the band; GCP cron's dom+dow OR semantics rule out
   "first Sunday"). Inert to `scheduled-ops.sh`; the P35.1a scheduler of
   record deploys the trigger.
7. **ADR-175** — the policy (PITR-clone parity, name-check deletion, AR-2,
   monthly export, lifecycle, relabel, voided-by rules); **ADR-081** gains
   the `## Status updates` append `- **Status:** Qualified by ADR-175
   (2026-10-02)` (S6R-24 — never an edit of the body); `docs/adr/README.md`
   regenerated.
8. **Pointers** — INFRA_RUNBOOK §9 (command tables + stop rules + rollbacks),
   GCP_DEPLOYMENT's relabel note naming the 09-15 dumps seed artefacts.
